taxonomic_note: Species-level learner concept, distinct from the other Elymus species in this batch. Hybrids and infraspecific variants can blur characters; use an intact mature spikelet and do not force a hybrid/intermediate into either species.
look_here_first: VIRGINIA WILDRYE (Elymus virginicus): first inspect the BASES of the paired GLUMES around one mature spikelet: they are often pale, hard and spread outward like a U. Its seed spike generally stays upright, comparatively compact, with shorter/straighter awns. CANADA typically nods with longer spreading awns and straighter, V-like glume bases. Photograph BOTH the entire head and its glumes—hybrids make single clues unreliable.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Calvin-approved Master Plant Pool (Elymus canadensis: 3 source flags; Elymus virginicus: 2) and existing canonical Elymus genus comparison lesson
project_inclusion.range_basis: No BONAP/NAPA-first three-target-county audit completed for this curation batch. Source-pool admission is independent of range certification; no native metrics credit.

best_field_traits: 1 · STRAIGHT SPIKE: terminal multiflowered seed SPIKE usually stays upright through maturity and may be partially included in the upper sheath.
2 · BONY U GLUMES: inspect one rachis node on a mature spike. Bases of paired outer glumes often turn outward, look pale and strongly hardened U-like.
3 · SHORTER STRAIGHTER AWNS: generally less divergent/long than Canada wildrye but ranges overlap.
4 · EACH NODE: commonly two or more multiflowered spikelets sit along central rachis; do NOT mistake their separate awns for a panicle.
5 · COLLAR: small auricles clasp culm; membranous ligule and overlapping leaf characters support Elymus genus, not species.
6 · Hybrids with E. canadensis known, so no claim of certain species from erect posture alone. Watch source-labelled montane/blue wildrye and barley look-alikes.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Versus E. canadensis: glume bases usually pale, thickened and U-bowed, with a more erect, compact spike and shorter, less divergent awns. E. canadensis tends to nod with longer outward-spreading awns and glume bases that are not distinctly bowed. Intermediate plants and hybrids require additional examination.
morphology_keys.glume_base: Glume pair typically hardens pale/whitish at the foot and BOWS noticeably away from the rachis node, creating a U-like divergence at the base. Photograph at high resolution with a millimeter ruler; source-labelled Montana macro confirms gross photographed outline, but an entire local spike is still needed.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Versus E. canadensis: glume bases usually pale, thickened and U-bowed, with a more erect, compact spike and shorter, less divergent awns. E. canadensis tends to nod with longer outward-spreading awns and glume bases that are not distinctly bowed. Intermediate plants and hybrids require additional examination.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare several mature attached rachis nodes from each species; photograph overall seed-spike profile too.
field_matrix.this_species: VIRGINIA: erect compact mature spike, often partly sheathed, shorter straighter awns; characteristic PALE HARD U-BOWED outer glume bases.
field_matrix.look_alike: CANADA: usually drooping, awns long/diffuse and glume bases narrow and straighter.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Use glume-base U vs V and posture together; do not force hybrid populations.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Determine spike vs branching PANICLE: look for continuous crowded rachis nodes with MULTIPLE florets in each spikelet.
field_matrix.this_species: VIRGINIA has a single terminal unbranched SPIKE with multiflowered spikelets attached at successive rachis nodes, each spikelet enclosed by glumes and containing several awned lemmas.
field_matrix.look_alike: Wintergrass has loose branching panicle of ONE-flowered hardened spikelets, each floret with ONE extremely long twisted awn and a sharp callus.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Multi-flowered spikelets along one central SPIKE = Elymus; isolated one-flowered grains along branching PANICLE = Nassella.

field_matrix.taxon: Barley or foxtail barley · Hordeum spp.
field_matrix.where_to_look: At one central rachis node check the number, shape and length of attached spikelets and whether multiple florets occur.
field_matrix.this_species: Elymus usually two (sometimes more) multi-FLOWERED spikelets per node, with relatively clear narrow glumes and awned lemmas.
field_matrix.look_alike: Hordeum often has distinct groups of 3 spikelets per rachis node, with very conspicuous long bristles and commonly ONE flower per spikelet.
field_matrix.quick_rule: A bristly whole head is not enough. Compare the cluster of spikelets/floret count on one attached node.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Inspect leaf auricles, actual glume basal width and spikelet floret number, then use regional dichotomous key.
field_matrix.this_species: VIRGINIA typically has a more upright, compact mature spike and pale, hard, outward-bowed U-shaped glume bases; verify several mature attached spikelets.
field_matrix.look_alike: Elymus glaucus, other wildryes and Canada × Virginia intermediate crosses overlap in habit and awns.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Contradictory morphology → Elymus sp., do not force two-species classification.

not_reliable_alone: One nodding or upright head without mature glume bases — posture can change with drying, wind and variation.
Awn color, long-awn bristliness, panicle size or leaf blade width alone.
One damaged or immature spikelet without its intact lower glume bases.
A vegetative leaf/auricle photo; sufficient for Elymus genus orientation but not these species.
Assuming the Montana source-labelled photos constitute a Hays County voucher, or that both species have passed the separate target-zone native certification.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Virginia wildrye — the bony U-base is the important picture
steps: Panel 8 (index 7): begin at Bob Harms's connected fibrous root crown and trace the same original plate to flowering culms; this is real Central Texas root-to-spike evidence, not a Hays voucher.

Panel 10 (index 9): follow the central unbranched spike rachis and awned flowering units. Photograph two attached mature nodes of a fresh plant with a 1-mm ruler before counting the paired multiflowered spikelets.
Panel 1 (index 0): inspect the pale, outward-bowed glume bases in Matt Lavin's actual Virginia wildrye close-up. These are glumes, not lemma awns, and the photo does not measure a Hays County plant.

Panel 2 (index 1) is an external Canada wildrye glume comparison with a structured depicts identity conflict; panel 5 (index 4) illustrates the often nodding Canada head. Neither settles hybrid identity.

Open the inner blade–sheath junction on the same fresh plant and measure the short true membranous ligule and clasping auricles separately. For reproductive confirmation separate a mature glume, lemma body, palea and terminal lemma awn with scale.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Use mature attached glume bases plus spikelet arrangement and overall head habit together; the source-identified Montana glume image and the Texas root-to-spike plate fill different photo roles. Keep ambiguous hybrids as Elymus sp.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Canada comparison macro has an unresolved structured depicts/source-identity discrepancy. The broad Montana Virginia habitat image (panel 6/index 5) is not a diagnostic spike macro. Native target-zone and hybrid holds remain unchanged.

field_id_finish_pass.look_here_first: Virginia wildrye: inspect several MATURE attached rachis nodes for paired multiflowered spikelets and pale, thickened glume bases that bow outward like a U. An upright compact spike with shorter, less-divergent awns supports the ID; head posture alone is not decisive against Canada wildrye or intermediates.
crew_field_check: Photograph one whole attached mature spike from base to tip with a centimeter ruler, showing its posture relative to the upper sheath.
At 10–20×, photograph two separate intact rachis nodes with paired spikelets and their outer glumes, using a 1-mm scale; label the rachis, glumes and lemma awns only where visible.
Measure and record glume basal shape and awn length from the same specimen rather than applying an unverified photo-based cutoff; compare multiple mature nodes with Canada wildrye.
Expose a leaf collar to show the small auricles and membranous ligule; these support Elymus, not a Virginia-versus-Canada species ID.
If head posture, glume-base curvature and awn spread conflict, retain Elymus sp. pending voucher/hybrid review.

lookalike_separation.check: Canada more often has a nodding open mature spike, long outward-spreading awns and narrow relatively straight V-like glume bases; compare several attached nodes because forms can hybridize.
Barleys often have three spikelets at a rachis node and commonly one floret per spikelet; Elymus typically has paired multiflowered spikelets.
Texas wintergrass has a branched panicle with single-flowered sharp-callused awned spikelets, not one central spike with multiflowered spikelets.

diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.look_here_first: At two attached mature spike nodes, inspect paired multi-flowered spikelets and the hard, pale, often outward-bowed U-shaped glume bases. The spike commonly stays upright and may remain partly enclosed by the flag sheath; do not use erectness alone to exclude hybrids.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.growth_form: Cool-season tufted perennial without obvious rhizomes; culms approximately 60–120 cm in GrassBase. Small clasping auricles; true membranous ligule generally under 1 mm.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.spikelet_glume_lemma_awn: Rachis nodes commonly carry paired sessile spikelets, each approximately 10–15 mm with 2–6 florets depending on treatment. Paired glumes approximately 7–15 mm, 3–5-veined, with hard often bowed basal portion and glume awns; lemma bodies approximately 8–10 mm, 5–7-veined, each with a single terminal awn often 5–25 mm. Measure body separately from awn and examine several nodes; regional/varietal ranges overlap.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.lookalikes: Elymus canadensis commonly nods with more spreading long awns and straighter V-shaped glume bases, but hybrids and variants require voucher review. Hordeum has three usually one-flowered spikelets at a node; Elymus paired spikelets are multi-flowered. Elymus curvatus can have very short lemma awns.
precise_photo_arrow_gaps: Hays-area rooted tuft plus entire mature spike and flag sheath, with centimeter ruler; verify plant and source identity.
Two intact attached rachis nodes photographed at 10–20× with 1-mm scale; arrow the actual U-bowed hardened glume bases, spikelet pair and rachis.
Separate glume body versus glume awn and lemma body versus lemma awn in a 1-mm-scaled dissection; record node-to-node variation.
True ligule membrane (<1 mm) and clasping auricles at the same leaf collar with 1-mm scale; do not infer from sheath hairs.
Same-angle vouchered E. canadensis mature spike and glume bases; preserve unresolved hybrid/range status.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Preserve two Matt Lavin CC BY-SA 2.0 images, annotations and unresolved county/hybrid decisions. Only mark FINISHED after taxon-verified measured rachis/glume/lemma and collar photographs, exact arrow targets, individual public rights, and live-site QA.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.evidence_scope: Published regional morphology, not new measurements from the two archived images. Source treatments include species/variety variation.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — U-SHAPED GLUME BASES
field_id_short_tiles.short: On several attached mature spike nodes, look for hard pale glume bases bowing outward like a U.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow one upright, relatively compact flowering spike (often partly enclosed by its upper leaf sheath) and magnify two attached rachis nodes. The paired multiflowered spikelets and thickened, often outward-bowed glume bases are stronger evidence than head posture. A Texas A&M comparison describes Canada wildrye as more often nodding with narrower V-like glume bases; hybrids and regional variants can blur both clues. Existing regional source photographs do not constitute a measured Hays voucher. Photo route: panel 1 (index 0) shows source-identified curved glume bases, while panels 10–11 (indices 9–10) show actual Texas flowering spikes; the glume macro is not a measured Hays voucher.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD CUE — LOCAL MEASURED GLUME-BASE MACRO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · TUFT, LIGULE AND AURICLES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Cool-season tufted perennial, culms about 60–120 cm; membranous ligule 0–1 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Trace an actual rooted shoot: published GrassBase describes a perennial clump, without a creeping rhizome. At the blade/sheath junction inspect the very short membranous ligule and often clasping, curved auricles; these support an Elymus identification, not a definitive separation from E. canadensis. Source photographs show connected roots and flowering culms, but a fresh same-voucher Hays collar with a 1-mm ruler remains unverified. Photo route: panel 8 (index 7) documents connected roots and flowering culms on a Central Texas Bob Harms plate; panel 7 (index 6) shows foliage. Neither image proves a 0–1 mm inner ligule or auricles at a measured collar.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED MEASUREMENTS — TRUE COLLAR MACRO NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT SPIKELETS AND FLORETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Usually 2–3 sessile spikelets per rachis node, each 10–15 mm with several florets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Go Botany documents 2–3 spikelets per node and 10–15 mm spikelet bodies. At 10–20× count actual spikelets at ONE node, then open ONE spikelet to find multiple florets; do not count awns as florets. Measure the body without awns and keep the node attached. Hordeum little barley instead has three usually one-flowered spikelets per node, central fertile and lateral often reduced. Photo route: panels 10–11 (indices 9–10) show the spike axis and awned units; panel 1 (index 0) gives an external glume-base close-up. Counting florets and measuring attached node parts still requires a new scaled dissection.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE-BASED ANATOMY — SAME-PLANT NODE SCALE MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES, LEMMA AND AWN ORIGIN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Glumes about 7–15 mm; fertile lemma body about 8–10 mm with one terminal awn often 5–25 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Go Botany reports both glumes 7–15 mm and a lemma awn 3–25 mm; Kew GrassBase describes a 5–25 mm principal lemma awn and a 5–7-veined lemma. Published ranges reflect different treatments and forms. Expose glume body, its awned tip, lemma body and terminal lemma awn separately on one mature dissection. The characteristic hard bowed glume base is not itself a lemma; do not draw anatomy arrows on hidden bracts. Photo route: panel 1 (index 0) illustrates paired curved glumes; panel 11 (index 10) is a flowering close-up, NOT a separated glume/lemma/palea dissection. Do not put microscopic lemma/awn arrows on hidden bracts.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED MORPHOLOGY — DISSECTED MEASURED PHOTO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Canada wildrye tends to nod; little barley has one-flowered spikelet triads; Texas wintergrass has a panicle.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Compare mature E. canadensis at the SAME stage: usually longer, spreading awns and straighter V-like glume bases, but E. virginicus × E. canadensis hybrids prevent certainty from one clue. H. pusillum has three one-flowered spikelets per rachis node, versus paired multiflowered Elymus. Nassella leucotricha has a branched panicle of single-flowered, sharply awned units. If attached glumes and head form disagree, retain Elymus sp. and a voucher. Photo route: Virginia panels 1 and 3 (indices 0,2) versus Canada panels 2 and 5 (indices 1,4). The Canada close-up carries a structured depicts/identity discrepancy and must be treated as a provisional comparison, not a voucher-confirmed species diagnostic.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COMPARISON KEY — MATCHED VOUCHER PHOTO NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE AND PHOTO HANDOFF
field_id_short_tiles.short: 11 existing teaching panels and 18 markers; measured local glume/ligule/lemma photos and site QA still outstanding.
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: same identified Hays-area rooted plant, complete spike and sheath with cm scale; two attached 1-mm-scaled mature nodes with true hard U-bowed glume bases; separately exposed glume, 8–10 mm lemma and its awn; in-focus 0–1 mm true ligule plus auricles; matched E. canadensis V-base specimen. NEEDS_SITE_QA: verify all eight current image records and their original individual CC BY-SA 2.0/Bob Harms credited educational permissions, preserved existing arrows against real pixels, source-label caveats, tile rendering and successful public deployment. Do not change unresolved county-native/hybrid status or claim FINISHED before measured evidence and rights/site QA. Public-readiness route: panels 8, 1, 2 and 10 (indices 7,0,1,9). Verify actual pixels and rights before certifying glume-base annotations; a measured local glume/ligule/lemma series and site QA are still outstanding.

grass_species_finalization_20261028.scope: Existing canonical Elymus virginicus only. Correct stale photo-install status and field-photo navigation; no image/arrow/rights, genus, family, taxonomy, county-range, site or Pages changes.
grass_species_finalization_20261028.look_here_first: On an attached mature spike inspect paired multiflowered spikelets and the pale hard glume bases, often curved outward in a U. An erect compact spike supports Virginia wildrye, but Canada wildrye and hybrids require several mature nodes, not posture alone.
grass_species_finalization_20261028.published_measurements_not_verified_from: Usually 2–3 spikelets per rachis node, spikelets about 10–15 mm, glumes roughly 7–15 mm, lemma bodies roughly 8–10 mm, terminal lemma awns often 5–25 mm, and short membranous ligule about 0–1 mm. Published treatments and regional forms vary; do not label these as pixel-measured.
